voyage.name: Arch of Galerius
voyage.content: The triumphal arch was dedicated in 303 AD to celebrate the victory of the tetrarch Galerius over the Sassanids.

voyage.name: Roman Forum
voyage.content: Excavations and an interesting museum underneath.

voyage.name: Rotunda
voyage.content: Started life as a Roman temple of Zeus, built by Caesar Galerius, and is almost as old as the Pantheon in Rome. The monument has a diameter of 24.5 m and its dome reaches a height of 30 m. It was converted into a Christian church during the Early Christian era, and its interior was decorated with magnificent mosaics. However some inside frescoes are a work of the British artist Alexander Rossi (1840-1916). In 1591 th

voyage.name: Saint Demetrios
voyage.content: Constructed in the mid-7th century on the ruins of a Roman bath complex, in honor of Demetrius, a Roman officer who was imprisoned and martyred here in 303 AD. An earlier small church, built on the site of martyrdom, burned down during the earthquake of 620 and a new large basilica was erected at expenses of Leontius, the Byzantine prefect of Illyricum and the Bishop of Thessaloniki. The new church of S. Demetrios be

voyage.name: Church of the Acheiropoietos
voyage.content: A 5th-century church. The surviving original decoration includes fine 5th-century Ionian capitals, the green Thessalian marble columns of the tribelon and fragments of 5th-century decorative mosaics. Early 13th-century frescoes adorn the southern side.

voyage.name: Latomou Monastery
voyage.content: A late 5th-century church, once part of a monastery. Many surviving elements of the Byzantine decoration are of high artistic quality, especially the 5th-century apse mosaic the Icon of Christ of Latomos. Under Ottoman rule, the building was converted into a mosque.

voyage.name: Hagia Sophia
voyage.content: A church from the 7th century, based on the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, with mosaics from the 9th century.

voyage.name: Panagia Chalkeon
voyage.content: An 11th-century church. The paintings are from the time the church was built, except a few from the 14th century.

voyage.name: Saint Catherine
voyage.content: Fragments of its interior decoration are dated to ca. 1315.

voyage.name: Saint Panteleimon
voyage.content: A church built in the 14th century. Few of the building's original wall paintings survive, but its architecture is striking.

voyage.name: Church of the Holy Apostles
voyage.content: The interior decoration consists of rich mosaics on the upper levels. Frescoes complete the decoration on the lower levels of the main church, but also on the narthex and one of the chapels.

voyage.name: Saint Nicholas Orphanos
voyage.content: A 14th-century church, particularly worth a look for its well-preserved frescoes. See if you can spot one of the turtles in the garden.

voyage.name: Church of the Saviour
voyage.content: A 14th-century chapel.

voyage.name: Vlatades Monastery
voyage.content: A monastery built in the 14th century.

voyage.name: Church of Prophet Elijah
voyage.content: A 14th-century church. Fragments of the church's original wall paintings survive.

voyage.name: Byzantine Bath
voyage.content: Baths from the 12th/13th century that functioned continuously until 1940.

voyage.name: White Tower
voyage.content: A 34 m fortified tower from the 16th-century, the primary symbol of the city. It was part of the city's erstwhilse Byzantine walls, and became a prison under the Ottomans. Today it houses a small museum dedicated to the history of the city, and viewpoints at the top. The exhibits are only in Greek, but the museum provides WiFi and an MP3-based audioguide.

voyage.name: Heptapyrgion
voyage.content: Medieval fort built by the Ottomans, overlooking the city from Thessaloniki's acropolis. The Greeks converted it into a prison which remained open until 1989.

voyage.name: Trigoniou tower
voyage.content: There is an observation deck just outside the tower, offering great views of the city.

voyage.name: Bey Hamam
voyage.content: Built in 1444 by sultan Murad II, it was the first Ottoman bath in Thessaloniki and the most important one still standing throughout Greece.

voyage.name: Bedesten
voyage.content: A historical Ottoman market for jewellery and precious materials

voyage.name: Alaca Imaret Mosque
voyage.content: A historic mosque completed in the 1480s, with an imaret (public charity kitchen).

voyage.name: Hamza Bey Mosque
voyage.content: A former mosque built in 1460. In modern times, a cinema operated in the premises for decades.

voyage.name: Eleftherias Square
voyage.content: In July 1942, during the Nazi occupation, all Jewish men aged 18 to 45 years old were brought here and were ordered to perform humiliating acts.

voyage.name: Thessaloniki Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: Andronikou st 6. Covers the history of Thessaloniki from prehistory to Roman times.

voyage.name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
voyage.content: Focuses on Early Christian life in the Byzantine Empire, with exhibits on churches, cities and Dwellings, cemeteries, castles and monastic communities. Declared best Museum of Europe in 2005.

voyage.name: Olympic Museum
voyage.content: Sports related.

voyage.name: Atatürk House
voyage.content: The house where Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was born.

voyage.name: State Museum of Contemporary Art, Thessaloniki
Museum of Ancient Greek, Byzantine, and Post Byzantine Musical Instruments
Folklife and Ethnological Museum of Macedonia and Thrace
Thessaloniki Zoological Garden
voyage.content: A small municipal zoo with many hilly climbs. The exhibited animals are mostly goats, sheep, ducks, deer, and peacocks. Admission is free.

voyage.name: Cultural Route public bus tour
voyage.content: OASTH launched a special “Cultural Route” to make the rich historical and cultural heritage of Thessaloniki more accessible. The bus departs from the White Tower for a 50-minute tour around the city's main historical and cultural monuments. The tour is supported by a telematics based audio-visual material (in Greek and English), as well as by printed leaflets (also in Greek and English).

voyage.name: Thessaloniki Concert Hall
voyage.content: The venue includes a main hall of 1,400 seats, designed by the Japanese architect Arata Isozaki and inaugurated on 2 January 2000. The Thessaloniki State Symphony Orchestra plays Italian Operas and works of Greek composers.

voyage.name: Waterland
voyage.content: A large water park near Tagarades Hill. Free bus service starting at the city centre.

voyage.name: Discovery Yachting
voyage.content: Bareboat charter or skippered sailing yacht, also night time tours.

voyage.name: Nautilia Yachting
voyage.content: Licensed by the Greek National Tourism Organization, organizes skippered or bareboat yacht charters with a wide range of monohulls and catamarans for sailing.

voyage.name: World Naked Bike Ride
voyage.content: A celebration of Cycling, Environment, Body Freedom.

voyage.name: Thessaloniki Film Festival
voyage.content: Lively and youth-oriented

voyage.name: Ianos bookshop
voyage.content: Books & art-objects, cultural events.

voyage.name: Modiano Market
voyage.content: The traditional central food market, with hundreds of stalls selling meat, fish, fruit, vegetables (sometimes cheek-by-jowl, an unnerving experience for North Americans), cheap clothes and shoes, flowers, herbs and spices, near Aristotele Square. The indoor portion is closed for an extensive renovation. It was supposed to reopen in 2021, but as of August 2022 the work is ongoing. The shops in the back alleys are stil

voyage.name: Kapani Market
voyage.content: The city's oldest market, with a wide variety of shops.

voyage.name: Chatzis
voyage.content: It is famous for its collection of Greek Asia Minor sweets (politika glyka) originating from Constantinople.

voyage.name: Terkenlis
voyage.content: It is famous for its variety of "tsoureki", a sweet bread much like challah or brioche but containing spices too, covered and filled with several combinations of chocolates, creams, and nuts.

voyage.name: Elenidis
voyage.content: It is considered the expert in "trigona" (triangles made of thin phyllo dough layers and filled with cream).

voyage.name: Choureál
voyage.content: Very popular for its profiterole

voyage.name: Evi Evan
voyage.content: A nice small place near the ancient market of Thessaloniki. Very cozy and nicely decorated. The personnel are very friendly and helpful and eager to make you feel welcome. Very nice place with traditional style and music. You will get nice plates and local drinks.

voyage.name: Verges Lagies
voyage.content: Reminiscent of old taverns from the 80s with very helpful staff and respect for the customer. Really nice charcoal grill food. Small bistro and worthwhile a try. Good quality for little money.

voyage.name: Pizza Chris
voyage.content: One of the nicest pizzas in Thessaloniki. Well made dough and incredible flavors. The pizza slices are only €1.50.

voyage.name: Tarantoúla
voyage.content: Nice place with good vegan food. This is the best place to enjoy vegan mezze in Thessaloniki. You can find a decently sized menu with several options to choose from. The space is very alternative but small with some outdoor seating and expect to have to wait for seating if you arrive at peak hours. The beet salad is fresh and delicious.

voyage.name: Nostimo - The Art In Taste
voyage.content: Very tasty homemade food with lots of vegetables from their garden. Friendly staff, affordable rates, nice and clean interiors

voyage.name: Ouzománia
voyage.content: This is a small tavern. One of the oldest ouzories. Kind staff and great atmosphere.

voyage.name: ΚΛΕΑ Fine Bakery
voyage.content: Cafe with light meals and takeaway.

voyage.name: Villa Luna
voyage.content: Ask to eat in the restaurant terrace - fantastic views at sunset.

voyage.name: Agora
voyage.content: Ouzo restaurant (ouzeri) in one of the most interesting old downtown areas.

voyage.name: To Manitari
voyage.content: Mediterranean cuisine, with an emphasis on seafood. Offers vegetarian options. Well-supplied with many regional Greek wines.

voyage.name: Omilos The Beach Club
voyage.content: Regional Greek ingredients.

voyage.name: Nea Diagonios
voyage.content: Here you can eat pork gyros and soutzoukakia from executive chef Ioannis Chantakis

voyage.name: Pire kai vradiazei
voyage.content: Great taverna, unique style, good food and some days (Th-Su) live music.

voyage.name: Toixo Toixo (Wall by Wall)
voyage.content: An hipster hang-out, nice atmosphere, very expensive for the quality.

voyage.name: Tsarouchas
voyage.content: For those with adventurous tastes, preferably go after a hard night's drinking, for a "patsás" (tripe) soup, a delicious way to prevent a hangover.

voyage.name: Heavy Melon
voyage.content: Traditional Greek, Mediterranean and Middle-Eastern recipes. Also, a selection of desserts.

voyage.name: Goody's
voyage.content: It is the Greek fast-food chain. You will find classic hamburgers, also souvlaki, pasta and salads.

voyage.name: Apo Dyo Horia
voyage.content: Cretan and Pontian restaurant. Here, order raki rather than ouzo or tsipouro.

voyage.name: Kamaras
voyage.content: Great traditional dishes.

voyage.name: Lila Cafe Bistro
voyage.content: Traditional pies and sweets, croissant and dishes accompany the coffee or your drink. Porcelain miniatures and collective drinks are available for original gifts.

voyage.name: Myrsini
voyage.content: Good Cretan restaurant.

voyage.name: Pizza da Pepe
voyage.content: For the best pizzas in town head here.

voyage.name: Tombourlika
voyage.content: Great traditional ouzeri, with fresh fish and meat dishes and live rembetico music.

voyage.name: Odos Aristotelous
voyage.content: Most Salonicans know it as the "Lepen".

voyage.name: Zythos-Dore
voyage.content: An upmarket brasserie with a wide range of specialties and interesting ambiance.

voyage.name: Mylos Club
voyage.content: Hosting concerts, events, exhibitions, music bands, famous Greek artists etc. Venue can change. Check their page on Facebook.

voyage.name: Little Big House Hostel
voyage.price: €17 for bed in 6-person dorm, €19 for bed in 4-person dorm
voyage.content: This is a new hostel in Thessaloniki run by a brother and sister who are hosts. They have five rooms in a reconstructed house, each room with private bathroom and kitchenette and big lockers. There is also a common room and kitchen, and a nice, cozy garden area with tables and chairs. Welcome drink, maps of the city, wifi and linens, tea and coffee, all free. Laundry and breakfast for €2.

voyage.name: Backpackers Refuge
voyage.content: Near the city centre (5-min bus ride) and the water front (7 min on foot) is well connected to the train station, bus station and the airport. 24 hr hot water, free linen, washing machine, kitchen, free city map, info available about Thess, and activities in northern Greece. Pick up and other transport options, free internet. Only a small capacity and advanced booking is recommended-staff is not present around the cl

voyage.name: The Tourist Hotel
voyage.price: €75 for a double room including breakfast
voyage.content: 2-star hotel, cheap, clean and welcoming. Single, double or triple rooms. Free WiFi. Parking with an extra charge of €15 per day.

voyage.name: Rex Hotel
voyage.content: Cheap hotel opposite the train station towards the centre. Only a 5-min walk from train station. Not great, but adequate.

voyage.name: Hotel Acropoli
voyage.price: A triple costs €80 or €60 for a double
voyage.content: Close to the train station. Clean but shabby rooms, most with a balcony.

voyage.name: Alexandria Hotel
voyage.content: Bang in the centre of Egnatia Str., with easy bus connections. Friendly staff. Price includes private bathroom, A/C, WiFi, fridge and TV. Snacks and laundry for extra charge.

voyage.name: RentRooms Thessaloniki
voyage.content: Travellers and backpackers hostel. Nice & clean rooms and dorms with balconies. Cafeteria garden for drinks and snacks near a green park. It is in city centre's university side, overlooking "Rotonda" UNESCO World Heritage Roman monument site. Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff really helpful. Available breakfast and bicycles. Free internet stations, WiFi in rooms and common areas.

voyage.name: Heaven Hotel
voyage.content: Between the hills of Tagarades with panoramic views of the city and Thermaico's gulf.

voyage.name: Zaliki Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in Thessaloniki city centre in a neo-classical building offering free wi-fi, free parking and free pick-up from airport.

voyage.name: El Greco Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in the heart of Thessaloniki. Free parking lot, VIP taxi service and free WiFi.

voyage.name: City Hotel
voyage.content: 4 star.

voyage.name: Kinissi Palace
voyage.content: 4 star.

voyage.name: Rotonda
voyage.content: 3-star hotel entering the city of Thessaloniki. Free parking lot, VIP taxi service and free WiFi.

voyage.name: Le Palace
voyage.price: The price posted in the room is over €180, although it is possible to haggle down to as low as €60 including breakfast if business is slack
voyage.content: Very nice double rooms

voyage.name: Hotel Luxembourg
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in neoclassical building next to the Thessaloniki seaside and Aristotelous square

voyage.name: Hotel Olympia
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in the centre of Thessaloniki.

voyage.name: Hotel Anessis
voyage.content: 3-star hotel next to Thessaloniki seaside and port with free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Tobacco Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star boutique hotel (formerly a tobacco warehouse).

voyage.name: Capsis Hotel
voyage.content: 5 star.

voyage.name: Hotel Philippion
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in the heart of Seich-Sou Park, overlooking Thessaloniki and Thermaikos Golf.

voyage.name: Park Hotel
voyage.content: Good breakfast buffet and reasonable price near the old Administration building.

voyage.name: Hotel Byzantio
voyage.content: In an all-green setting with sparkling water from the surrounding mountains, a few metres from the water mills, on an area of .

voyage.name: Amalia Hotel
voyage.content: 2-star hotel, in the centre of Thessaloniki, close to Aristotelous Square, all rooms with balcony and free WiFi.

voyage.name: a.d. Imperial Palace Thessaloniki Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in the city centre in a neo-classical building offering free wi-fi, free parking and free pick-up from airport.

voyage.name: Electra Palace Hotel Thessaloniki
voyage.content: 5-star hotel in the heart of Thessaloniki. 130 rooms and 8 suites, some of them with a view of Aristotelous square and the sea. The "Orizontes Pool Bar & Restaurant" provides superb view of Thermaikos gulf.

voyage.name: Makedonia Palace
voyage.content: One of the most prestigious hotels in Thessaloniki, on the waterfront.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Thessaloniki
voyage.content: 5-star hotel with 2 ballrooms, 5 meeting rooms and 3 boardrooms. 2 km from the largest casino in Europe.

voyage.name: Porto Palace Hotel
voyage.content: At the west entrance of the city, near the new harbour/port. It has direct access to the new financial district and it is 5 min away from the city centre and the shopping area.

voyage.name: Domotel Les Lazaristes Hotel
voyage.content: Nearby the major cultural centre of the city. The State Museum of Contemporary Art inspired its design philosophy.

voyage.name: Mediterranean Palace Hotel
voyage.content: 5-star hotel with views of Thermaikos Bay.

voyage.name: NOA Hotel
voyage.content: Recognized as one of the best hotels in Thessaloniki city center, this modern 4-star boutique hotel features stylish rooms with sea views, fast Wi-Fi, and upscale design amenities.
